specs.title: Product Charter and RBAC
successCriteria: 100% of MVP capabilities are assigned to an accountable owner and acceptance scenario.
Every protected role has an explicit permission boundary before implementation begins.
No delivery task is admitted without an approved requirement and acceptance reference.

specs.title: AASTMT Policy Rulebook
successCriteria: Every registration decision identifies the governing policy version and reason.
All approved policy boundary examples can be evaluated deterministically.
No unresolved or unapproved policy value governs a student submission.

specs.title: Frontend Page Design, Storyboard, Accessibility and Functional Testing
successCriteria: All 27 route templates have approved page-design records and complete component, contract, E2E, accessibility, and visual test plans.
Critical journeys meet WCAG 2.2 AA requirements before release.
At least 90% of representative users complete registration in usability validation.

specs.title: Architecture and Engineering Principles
successCriteria: Every module dependency is explicit and free of cycles.
The system can run on at least two stateless application instances without changing user-visible behavior.
Every architecture exception is recorded with an approved decision and simpler alternatives considered.

specs.title: ERD and Data Lifecycle
successCriteria: All required uniqueness, capacity, relationship, and historical invariants are explicitly modeled.
Every imported or synthetic seeded academic record retains source provenance, and rebuilding the same seed version reproduces the same logical identities and academic values.
Migration, backup, and rollback requirements are documented before schema implementation.

specs.title: Domain Classes and API Contracts
successCriteria: Every declared endpoint interface records success, validation, authorization, conflict, and unexpected-error outcomes, or marks an inapplicable category with a reason.
No persistence-internal field or credential is part of a response contract; secret-bearing request fields are limited to the explicitly tested transient authentication and account-lifecycle inputs.
All externally visible dates, identifiers, pagination, and error formats are consistent.

specs.title: Quality, Security, Scalability, and Operations
successCriteria: Correctness invariants remain intact at target, double-target, and spike traffic.
Critical flows meet WCAG 2.2 AA and have no unresolved critical or high security finding.
Recovery evidence demonstrates an RPO of at most 5 minutes and RTO of at most 1 hour.

specs.title: Identity and Account Lifecycle
successCriteria: Authorized students and staff reach only their permitted context.
Account activation cannot claim an unknown or already-claimed institutional identity.
Authentication and recovery failures reveal no account-existence information.

specs.title: Academic Term and Student Profile
successCriteria: Registration availability is determined only by authoritative institutional time and approved windows.
Every eligibility decision uses a complete, sourced academic profile.
No overlapping active registration context can apply to the same student.

specs.title: Catalogue, Prerequisites, and Policy Administration
successCriteria: Invalid or cyclic catalogue relationships cannot be published.
Every published catalogue and policy version is immutable and auditable.
Administrators can preview and explain all validation failures before publication.

specs.title: Offerings, Groups, and Resources
successCriteria: Only complete and conflict-free groups become visible for registration.
Every visible group identifies capacity, staff, location, day, and time.
Capacity can never be configured below active enrollment.

specs.title: Eligibility and Subject Discovery
successCriteria: Every available or unavailable subject has an understandable reason.
Students can find relevant offerings within the approved response-time target.
No client-side action can turn an ineligible offering into an eligible one.

specs.title: Schedule Builder and Conflicts
successCriteria: Every overlapping meeting interval is identified before review.
Unresolved hard conflicts always block submission with accessible resolution guidance.
Equivalent calendar and chronological views contain the same schedule information.

specs.title: Schedule Recommendations
successCriteria: Every returned option contains exactly one viable group per selected course and no hard conflict.
Up to three options are ranked deterministically with understandable score reasons.
A no-solution or time-budget outcome never presents an incomplete schedule as valid.

specs.title: Registration Capacity and Concurrency
successCriteria: Concurrent submissions never overbook a group or duplicate an active course enrollment.
A multi-group registration is either fully accepted or has no committed enrollment changes.
Retrying the same submission never allocates an additional seat.

specs.title: Student Registration Records
successCriteria: Every accepted registration has a durable, uniquely identifiable receipt.
Rejected atomic submissions clearly state that no partial registration occurred.
Current and historical records remain understandable after later catalogue changes.

specs.title: Lecturer and Teaching Assistant Workspace
successCriteria: Staff can view only assignments and roster data within their current scope.
Lecturer and TA contexts use shared journeys without merging their permissions.
Availability changes never silently move a published class.

specs.title: Admin Operations, Audit, and Reporting
successCriteria: Every sensitive administrative mutation records actor, reason, time, and before/after context.
Normal administrative actions cannot bypass capacity or timetable invariants.
Operational information is timestamped, scoped, and distinguishable from stale or unavailable data.
